Here is the number that explains the Wild: 16-0. That's the five-on-five goal count with Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek on the ice over 191 minutes. They take 66% of the expected goals and create 4.02 per hour. Quinn Hughes put it plainly in Heather Rule's NHL.com recap: "Can't say it enough, I just feel like we can tilt the ice when they're out there."

Minnesota is 12-3-3 with 27 points and a seven-game point streak, and on Nov. 6 became the fastest team to 1,000 regular-season wins, per The Athletic's Michael Russo. Hughes sits on the top pair with either Jonas Brodin or Jared Spurgeon, both north of 60% of the chances.

Is it sustainable? Mostly. The Wild have 57.7% of the expected goals and create 3.77 per hour, elite numbers, and they've actually scored eight fewer goals than those chances usually bring. The bigger lift is in net: Jesper Wallstedt is .930 with 5.4 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Across the season the goaltending has saved about 11 goals more than expected, and our model counts about three points of luck. Some of that will fade.

Our numbers give Minnesota a 99% playoff chance, a 110-point pace and a better-than-even shot at the Central. Calvin Pickard starts the second half of a back-to-back against Tampa tonight.
headline: Minnesota's top line hasn't been scored on
